rawIngestions.titleRaw: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution. Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. Existing pruning strategies divide broadly into two categories: Quality-based methods assign a score to each partial solution and discard those predicted to ultimately lead to an incorrect final solution, while diversity-based methods select partial solutions that follow different reasoning trajectories and are therefore likely to cover different final solutions. The tension between these two objectives is an instance of exploration versus exploitation, yet little to no prior work on pruning exposes this trade-off directly, let alone optimizes it. In this paper, we introduce a pruning procedure that addresses this trade-off directly by optimizing pass@$k$ over the selected solution pool. In particular, it chooses the pool to maximize the probability that at least one of its partial solutions, when continued to completion, yields a correct answer. Because this objective simultaneously rewards high-quality partial solutions and penalizes redundancy among them, quality and diversity are naturally balanced by the criterion itself rather than through separate ad-hoc design choices. On eight open-weight reasoning models, our method outperforms existing quality-based and diversity-based pruning strategies. The gains are particularly pronounced when the pruning procedure keeps a moderate number of partial solutions for continued generation, highlighting the value of directly balancing quality and diversity during pruning.

payloadJson.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Constructing accurate and computationally tractable approximation spaces is a fundamental task in scientific computing. Partially trainable neural networks bridge fixed random features and fully adaptive representations. This paper quantifies a phase transition pattern in approximation bounds and observes analogous behavior in training errors: a rapid but smooth initial improvement followed by diminishing returns, with a sharper transition under greater initialization mismatch. Under polynomial spectral decay with exponent $α>1$ and leverage compatibility, we establish a squared $L_2$ approximation rate $\mathcal{O}((κ_P\log(m/δ)/m)^α)$ for two-layer networks of width $m$ and trainable proportion $P$, where $κ_P=(P/κ_1^*+(1-P)/κ_0^*)^{-1}$. The bound holds uniformly over the unit ball of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) with probability at least $1-δ$. The constants $κ_0^*$ and $κ_1^*$ quantify the fixed and trainable groups' sampling mismatches relative to the target RKHS. For spherical biased-ReLU features in dimension $d$, we verify these assumptions with $α=(d+2)/(d-1)$ and $κ_0^*=4\sqrt{2}τ(d+1)/d$ for initialization scale $τ\ge1$, and $κ_1^*=1$ under ridge leverage sampling. For $d=5$ and $τ=10$, a trainable proportion of approximately $4.1\%$ captures $90\%$ of the reduction in the approximation bound from $P=0$ to $P=1$. A structured three-layer example illustrates how a few trainable first-layer neurons exploit fixed downstream blocks through nonlinear composition. Numerical experiments across diverse settings, including networks with up to 15 layers, exhibit similar phase transitions in training errors.

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
rawIngestions.contentRaw: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions. At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision. The decision and confidence score need not be produced by the same model: for example, one agent may propose a decision, while a separate verifier agent evaluates it and outputs a correctness or safety score. Based on this information, we must decide whether to accept the AI decision automatically or consult an expert, such as a human auditor, who reviews the proposal and either accepts or corrects it. We formulate this task as an online constrained optimization problem in which the goal is to minimize the frequency of expert auditing while guaranteeing that the fraction of AI errors that go unaudited stays below a user-defined threshold. We derive a family of algorithms with provable error-control guarantees with no assumptions, including a method that is optimally efficient: it asymptotically attains the best achievable auditing rate for both adversarial and i.i.d. data streams. Experiments on screening harmful requests to large language models, qualitative text annotation, and data labeling show that our methods achieve valid error control in practice while substantially reducing the need for human auditing compared to baselines.

payloadJson.title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing

rawIngestions.titleRaw: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images. Proactive dataset-use auditing plants a shared signal in a dataset before release, then later checks whether that signal appears in a suspect model's generated outputs. Existing approaches often trade off verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability. We introduce $\textbf{SpectralCanary}$, which uses a smooth low-pass mask to blend a fixed canary image into every collection image while leaving captions unchanged and requiring neither auxiliary generation nor per-image optimization. A lightweight verifier detects the transferred signal in suspect-model outputs. Across eight tests on the Pokemon dataset and three realistic data transformations, spanning two architectures families, SpectralCanary achieves the highest average per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR ($91.1\%$) and fixed threshold model-level accuracy using 30 generations ($94.8\%$) among the evaluated methods. Across five datasets spanning artistic, medical, satellite, and fashion domains with SD3.5, SpectralCanary averages $92.4\%$ per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR while preserving the released images (SSIM $0.989$, LPIPS $0.022$) with a near-zero mean change FID (mean $Δ$FID $0.05$) across datasets. Matched-energy ablations on Pokemon and ROCOv2 support our design choice, low-frequency placement transfers more reliably compared to mid/high-frequency placement. Under the evaluated adaptive attacks, the most effective removal requires aggressive modification and incurs more than $25$ $Δ$FID points. These results identify low-frequency visual signals as effective carriers for collection-level T2I audit traces.

payloadJson.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis. The strongest prompted configuration reaches 0.477 accuracy on a stratified 1,000-ticket test subset, versus 0.879 for fine-tuned DistilBERT on the same tickets. Isotonic lowers expected calibration error without reliably improving discrimination: GPT-4o-mini few-shot has one confidence value before and after recalibration and correctness AUROC 0.500. We therefore report correctness AUROC and tie-aware risk-coverage area alongside ECE. At the analytically derived break-even probability 0.80, seven prompted configurations defer all tickets; Haiku few-shot routes only 19/1,000. An LLM-only agreement control and margin/entropy rejection baselines further separate calibration from discrimination. The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.

payloadJson.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification

- Linux: Fixed sandbox write denies lifting when a background command outlived the session
- Windows: Fixed PowerShell permission checks auto-approving some `Set-Location` or `cd` commands that target the current directory and carry extra arguments; these now prompt for approval

- Fixed MCP servers being reported as timed out, and staying failed in headless runs, when a macOS or Linux computer went to sleep while they were connecting
- Fixed HTTP MCP tool calls being sent twice when the connection closed mid-call; only read-only or idempotent tools are now retried
- Fixed a turn sometimes starting without an SDK MCP server's latest tools when a background task was running
- Fixed some "Autocompact is thrashing" errors in turns that read many PDF pages, images or other large tool results
- Fixed `/autocompact` in cloud sessions going back to the default window after the session restarted
- Fixed a conversation cleared with `/clear` sometimes coming back when a cloud or self-hosted runner session restarted
- Fixed `CLAUDE_STREAM_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS` being ignored in Claude apps gateway sessions
- Fixed telemetry from Claude Desktop sessions behind a Claude apps gateway being rejected when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` is set
- Fixed `/permissions` > Recently denied not showing the denied shell command, and auto mode's local classifier ignoring an approval from there when it checks a retried command; approving a row now names the command, not its description
- Fixed `/help` and the `/` command menu showing long model-facing descriptions for bundled skills such as `/claude-api` instead of their short descriptions
- Fixed subagent transcripts recording placeholder token usage and an empty stop reason for streamed responses
- Fixed model switches through the Agent SDK's `setModel()`, and apps built on it, being refused when the API took more than 5 seconds to confirm the model; Claude Code now waits up to 15 seconds
- Fixed a background command stopped through a connected app (such as the desktop app archiving an idle session) being reported to Claude as stopped by the user; the notice now names its output file
- Fixed WebFetch in Cowork cloud sessions reporting a tool error when a site answered with a 4xx status or a robots.txt refusal; it is now a normal result, as in local sessions
- Fixed write tools on a directly configured GitHub MCP server showing a form that closed without creating anything in the desktop app's Code tab
- Fixed Artifact tool reads failing with a connection reset when the server had closed a reused connection
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions with `--use-anthropic-git-proxy` committing a `.claude/settings.local.json` left in the clone by an earlier session
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed archiving or requeueing a session, or stopping the runner, during its checkout hook leaving the hook's processes running and the runner's slot held
- Improved recovery from unparseable tool calls: Claude Code now retries the call up to twice before ending the turn with an error
- Improved fork subagents launched together: each is now told which launch is its own, so forks are much less likely to try to start each other's work
- Improved browser sign-in: the success page now appears as soon as sign-in completes, without waiting for your account profile to load
- Improved web search errors in cloud and self-hosted runner sessions: a search refused with a 403 that gives a reason now shows that reason instead of a generic "Authentication error"
- Improved the time to the first reply in cloud sessions when one of the desktop app's MCP servers can't connect
- Improved Remote Control connect time for sessions whose transcript contains large pasted images or PDF reads
- Changed the notice Claude gets when the WebSearch budget is used up to also tell it not to query search engines in a browser or through computer use
- Changed the `axScreenReader` setting and `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER` in a settings `env` block to apply only from user, managed or `--settings` settings (since 2.1.305)
- Self-hosted runner: Changed checkout hooks to be stopped after 30 minutes by default, failing the session's setup; if yours needs longer, raise `--checkout-hook-timeout-min` or set it to `0`
- Self-hosted runner: Changed the certificate file built for Anthropic-managed git to filter its trusted certificates as the CLI does; a `[runner:warn]` line gives the number left out
- [VSCode] Added a notice on the microphone button when voice dictation stops by itself (15 seconds without recognized speech, or the 2-minute limit), saying why and that the text so far is kept
- [VSCode] Fixed a long prompt expanded with Show more covering the whole chat panel: a pinned prompt is now capped at 40% of the panel and scrolls
- [VSCode] Fixed part of a list item or table cell with LaTeX math pasting as a new list or table in rich text editors
- [VSCode] Fixed dictation failing behind a TLS-inspecting proxy when `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is set only in `~/.claude/settings.json`; it now also follows `CLAUDE_CODE_CERT_STORE`
- [VSCode] Changed the "still open somewhere else" notice to also cover a Claude process left over from an extension restart, which usually ends on its own within about 10 minutes
- [VSCode] Changed voice dictation to filter its trusted certificates as the CLI does
- [VSCode] Changed the extension's own requests to filter their trusted certificates as the CLI does, and to trust the `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` file named in the environment or in user settings
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed the repository picker saying "No repositories match" while a search was still running; it now shows "Searching…" until the results arrive
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed the "Waiting for a runner" status on self-hosted environments being cut off; with on-demand runners it now counts up from your last message and shows failed attempts
- [Code Review] Added `@claude review stop` (also `off` and `pause`) to Code Review, ending an `@claude review always` subscription on a pull request without starting a new review

rawIngestions.contentRaw: # Release v5.20.0 ## New Model additions ### Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/muse_spark) | [Blog Post](http://hf.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open) * Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in [#49644](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49644) ### Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so it loads without `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/bailing_hybrid) * [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in [#49446](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49446) ### Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is *canvas M-RoPE*: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a `(temporal, height, width)` position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. * Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in [#48979](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48979#top) ### UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/unlimited_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.23050 (the docs link only the Hugging Face papers page, "Unlock OCR Works" is not given an arXiv link, so this is the paper URL provided)) * Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in [#46836](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46836) ### UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/moss_transcribe_diarize) * Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in [#48386](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48386) ## Breaking changes 🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨 Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from `cache_utils.py` (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API. * 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead. * 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin The minimum `kernels` version is now 0.17.2, which allows `use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL` so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade `kernels` to 0.17.2 or later. * 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc A new `SubConfigSpec` centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. Custom or existing nested configs may need to be updated to declare their sub-configs through this mechanism. * :rotating_light: SubConfigSpec for centralized init of subconfigs (#48282) by @zucchini-nlp The LUKE and mLUKE tokenizers now treat entity special tokens such as `` as special tokens (not split, honored by `skip_special_tokens`, normalized) while keeping the same spacing as regular vocabulary tokens when decoding. Tokenization and decoding output involving these tokens may therefore differ from before, so check any code or saved outputs that depend on the old behavior. * 🚨🚨🚨 luke fixe (#48408) by @itazap ## Exporters Transformers exporters now support quantization directly during export across Dynamo, ONNX, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch. The new unified quantization API integrates PT2E, ONNX Runtime, and NNCF quantizers, enabling static and dynamic quantization as well as weight-only compression (INT8/INT4), with configurable calibration workflows. This makes it easier to export optimized models for efficient inference across different backends. For more information see the docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/exporters_quantization ## Parallelization This release improves distributed training and inference. FSDP × TP model and optimizer checkpoints can now be saved and loaded across different parallel configurations, and expert-parallel dispatch, tensor-parallel plans, static-cache `generate()`, and the caching allocator's byte count were fixed. Tied LM heads in composite models now get their own TP plan entry, `enable_expert_parallel` applies the EP plan alone again, TPU loading uses the `tor * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading, Optimizer (#49256) by @michaelbenayoun in [#49256] * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading (#48802) by @michaelbenayoun in [#48802] * Don't set a device per rank for gloo tensor-parallel tests (#49636) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49636] * fix(distributed): keep enable_expert_parallel as EP alone (#49633) by @dacorvo in [#49633] * Fix a port allocation race in FSDP tests (#49455) by @icavan in [#49455] * Expert-parallel dispatch hands the experts the received rows, not the all-to-all's pending result (#49421) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49421] * Fix static-cache generate() with host-side inputs and under TP (#49317) by @dacorvo in [#49317] * Composite lm head tp plan (#49080) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49080] * Fix: use torch.accelerator device APIs so TP loading works again on TPU (#49502) by @tengomucho in [#49502] * Count ep and fsdp in caching_allocator_warmup byte calculation (#49384) by @3outeille in [#49384] * Do not wrap the model in FSDP for expert-parallel token dispatch (#49383) by @3outeille in [#49383] ## Generation This release fixes static-cache `generate()` bugs with host-side inputs and under tensor parallelism. It also speeds up Whisper generation on TPU by cutting device syncs and recompilation, and fixes Whisper batched timestamp decoding for tensor and NumPy inputs. release.body: # Release v5.20.0 ## New Model additions ### Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/muse_spark) | [Blog Post](http://hf.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open) * Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in [#49644](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49644) ### Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so it loads without `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/bailing_hybrid) * [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in [#49446](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49446) ### Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is *canvas M-RoPE*: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a `(temporal, height, width)` position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. * Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in [#48979](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48979#top) ### UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/unlimited_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.23050 (the docs link only the Hugging Face papers page, "Unlock OCR Works" is not given an arXiv link, so this is the paper URL provided)) * Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in [#46836](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46836) ### UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/moss_transcribe_diarize) * Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in [#48386](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48386) ## Breaking changes 🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨 Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from `cache_utils.py` (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API. * 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead. * 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin The minimum `kernels` version is now 0.17.2, which allows `use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL` so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade `kernels` to 0.17.2 or later. * 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc A new `SubConfigSpec` centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. The new unified quantization API integrates PT2E, ONNX Runtime, and NNCF quantizers, enabling static and dynamic quantization as well as weight-only compression (INT8/INT4), with configurable calibration workflows. rawIngestions.titleRaw: ollama/ollama v0.40.9 released
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
## Speech

Ollama can now generate [speech](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/speech) with Phonon on Apple Silicon. `ollama run` plays text or a chat model's reply aloud as the audio is generated, and apps can stream audio through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint.

```sh
ollama run phonon "Hello from Ollama."
```

## d3 decision models

[d3](https://ollama.com/library/d3) brings vLLM Semantic Router's decision models to Ollama. Give a model text, structured state, or an image, and ask it to classify, answer yes or no, or score options with probabilities. The family includes 2B, 4B, 9B, and 27B sizes.

```sh
ollama run d3 "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"
```

## Flint on Linux and Windows

[Flint](https://ollama.com/library/flint) now runs on Linux and Windows as well as macOS.

## Other improvements

- Streaming OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages requests now report generation failures instead of ending silently after partial output.
- `ollama launch` now passes cloud models' context lengths and capabilities to coding tools, fixing incorrect context and compaction settings.
- Anthropic-compatible web search now uses the model's supported thinking setting in follow-up requests, preventing avoidable failures.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.8...v0.40.9

* [pplx-decider](https://ollama.com/library/pplx-decider) is a 27B decision model from Perplexity, fine-tuned from

* Continuing an OpenAI-compatible Responses conversation no longer fails when switching between models with and without
thinking, or when the history contains another provider's compaction items
* Fixed streaming Responses requests where client tool calls (e.g. Codex with web search) could emit before open
reasoning items, producing misordered/duplicate tool call events
* Requests routed to remote models are now cancelled on ollama.com when the client disconnects, instead of continuing
to run
* `ollama show` now reports which renderer and parser a model uses and where its chat template comes from; the API
exposes the same values in new `renderer`, `parser`, and `template_source` fields
* More draft models now work with speculative decoding: llama-server infers the draft type automatically instead of
requiring Ollama to identify it
* `ollama launch claude` now clamps `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` to Claude Code's supported range, avoiding a
"window too large" warning
* Updated llama.cpp and MLX

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Show HN: AgentState – Lightweight state manager for multi-agent AI workflows
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
AgentState to solve a problem I kept running into: managing state for multi-agent AI systems is surprisingly hard. When you have multiple AI agents that need to coordinate, persist their state, and query each other's status, you typically end up with a mess of Redis/Postgres setups, custom queuing, and manual synchronization code.

The whole thing is ~3MB, written in Rust for performance and safety, runs in Docker, and handles 1000+ ops/sec. I've been running it in production for AI workflows and it's been rock solid.

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Show HN: ML Blocks – Deploy multimodal AI workflows without code
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
Hey everyone,

ML Blocks is a node-based workflow builder to create multi-modal AI workflows without writing any code.

You connect blocks that call various visual models like GPT4v, Segment Anything, Dino etc. along with basic image processing blocks like resize, invert color, blur, crop, and several others.

The idea is to make it easier to deploy multi-step image processing workflows, without needing to spin up endless custom OpenCV cloud functions to glue together AI models. Usually, even if you're using cloud inference servers like Replicate, you still need to write your own image processing code to pre and post-process images in your pipeline. When you're trying to move fast, that's just unnecessary overhead.

With ML Blocks, you can build a workflow and deploy the whole thing as a single API. AFAIK, ML Blocks is the only end-to-end workflow builder built specifically for image processing.

If you're curious, our models run on Replicate, HuggingFace & Modal Labs cloud GPUs and we use React Flow for the node UX.
